discovery_method: procedures/workflows/runbooks sweep (WebSearch+WebFetch) — multi-step PROCEDURES, PIPELINES, RUNBOOKS, and WORKFLOWS that are themselves capabilities: dbt models, Airflow/Dagster/Prefect DAG patterns, CI/CD pipelines, Terraform modules, Ansible roles, incident-response runbooks, SOAR/security playbooks, RPA procedures, ETL recipes, agent workflow templates (CrewAI/AutoGen/LangGraph), prompt-chain/pipeline templates (DSPy modules), and business SOPs (KYC/invoicing/onboarding).
governance: CANDIDATES ONLY — discovery is not trust. No row here is an active capability; each must pass the seeder's gap/lift screen, then human/eval gates, before any promotion. Source URLs are as reported and were spot-verified via WebFetch where noted; license/verify_note flags carried verbatim. serves_truth=false for everything downstream. Determinism ceilings reflect the slice rule: deterministic pipelines (declarative DAGs / IaC / compiled rules) ~0.85, agentic/LLM-orchestrated procedures ~0.4.

candidates.intent: Author a layered dbt ELT transformation (sources -> staging -> intermediate -> marts) with ref()/source() lineage, materializations, and dependency-ordered builds compiled to warehouse SQL.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot resolve a multi-model DAG, topologically order dependent transforms, or guarantee idempotent re-runs against a live warehouse; it emits one-off SQL that breaks on the next model.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: dbt compiles ref()/source() into a deterministic dependency graph and orders/materializes builds; the LLM only writes per-model SQL while dbt owns ordering, state, and incremental logic.
candidates.verify_note: dbt is the de-facto ELT transformation framework; ref()/source() DAG resolution and materializations are deterministic. License Apache-2.0; confirm pin.

candidates.intent: Apply battle-tested SQL transform macros (surrogate keys, deduplicate, pivot/unpivot, date_spine, union_relations, get_column_values) inside dbt models.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model hand-writing surrogate-key/dedupe/pivot SQL drifts per dialect and silently breaks on edge cases (nulls, ties, dialect quoting).
candidates.lift_hypothesis: dbt_utils provides dialect-aware, widely-tested macros so the transform is generated deterministically rather than improvised; structural because SQL-generation rules are model-independent.
candidates.verify_note: Most-installed dbt package (the 'swiss army knife'); macros are deterministic SQL generators. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Run Great-Expectations-style declarative data-quality tests inside a dbt run (column value ranges, regex match, freshness, distribution, multi-column relationships).
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot execute statistical/freshness assertions against live table data; it can only guess whether data is valid.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Provides 40+ deterministic data-quality assertions compiled to SQL and run against real rows, returning pass/fail + failing samples; durable because the assertion catalog is model-independent.
candidates.verify_note: Cited as 'the package every project needs'; 40+ tests. License Apache-2.0; confirm.

candidates.intent: Capture slowly-changing-dimension (SCD Type 2) history of a source table via dbt snapshots with check/timestamp strategies producing valid_from/valid_to records.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: SCD2 history tracking requires comparing current vs prior state across runs and persisting validity windows — a model has no run-to-run state.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: dbt snapshots deterministically diff source against stored history and write SCD2 validity windows; structural because the merge logic is model-independent.
candidates.verify_note: Core dbt feature; deterministic merge. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Define an Airflow DAG that extracts to S3, stages, loads to Redshift, and runs data-quality checks, with task dependencies, retries, and backfill.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot schedule, order, retry, or backfill a dependent multi-task pipeline against live systems; it loses state between steps.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Airflow's scheduler executes the declared task DAG with retries, dependencies, and backfill deterministically; the model only authors task code.
candidates.verify_note: ETL/ELT is the dominant Airflow use case (90% of 2023 survey); DAG scheduling is deterministic, leaf transforms may vary. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Use a community Airflow provider operator/hook (1000+: S3, BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres, GCS, dbt, Spark) to integrate a third-party system as a typed DAG task.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Hand-coding each integration (auth, pagination, retries, idempotency) per provider is error-prone and a model reinvents brittle glue each time.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: 1000+ maintained operators/hooks encapsulate auth and idempotent calls behind a typed interface; structural because the integration contracts are model-independent.
candidates.verify_note: Airflow has 1000+ community operators per official docs. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Build an ETL pipeline with Airflow TaskFlow API (@task decorators) passing data via XCom between extract/transform/load Python functions with automatic dependency inference.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot wire data-passing, dependency inference, and scheduling between Python steps that must run on a managed executor.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: TaskFlow deterministically infers dependencies from function return/args and manages XCom data passing and scheduling.
candidates.verify_note: TaskFlow is the canonical modern Airflow authoring pattern. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Declare data assets in code as @asset functions with explicit upstream dependencies; Dagster materializes them in dependency order with built-in lineage, partitioning, and versioning.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot maintain data-aware asset lineage, partition state, or dependency-ordered materialization across runs.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Dagster's data-aware model resolves asset dependencies and partitions deterministically and tracks lineage/versioning; the model only writes per-asset compute.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: Dagster's software-defined assets define data dependencies explicitly with built-in lineage/versioning. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Package a Prefect flow as a deployment with a storage block + infrastructure block (Docker, Kubernetes, ECS, Lambda, Azure) and a schedule, enabling reproducible remote runs.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot configure storage+infra+schedule blocks that reproducibly run a flow on remote infrastructure with correct serialization.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Prefect deployments deterministically bind flow code to storage/infra/schedule blocks for reproducible remote execution; the orchestrator owns scheduling and retries.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via WebFetch: repo demonstrates Docker/K8s/ECS/Lambda/Azure/GitHub-storage/scheduled/event-driven patterns. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Orchestrate a Python data pipeline as a Prefect @flow of @tasks with automatic retries, caching, concurrency limits, and state-based control.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot manage task-level retries, result caching, and concurrency across a running pipeline; it has no execution state.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Prefect's runtime applies retries/caching/concurrency deterministically by policy while the model authors task bodies.
candidates.verify_note: Prefect task-based orchestration with retries/caching is core; License Apache-2.0; confirm pin.

candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot compute a correct multi-AZ subnet/route/gateway topology, diff it against live cloud state, or apply it idempotently.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: The module encodes a correct, idempotent VPC topology; terraform plan/apply deterministically reconciles desired vs actual state. Structural: cloud resource graphs are model-independent.

candidates.intent: Stand up an Amazon EKS cluster (control plane, managed node groups, IRSA, add-ons, security groups) declaratively via the official terraform-aws-eks module.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Provisioning a correct EKS cluster requires coordinating dozens of interdependent resources (IRSA, OIDC, node groups, add-ons) a model cannot order or reconcile against live state.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: The module encodes the full EKS resource graph; terraform reconciles it idempotently. Durable because the AWS EKS resource contract is model-independent.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via GitHub: terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-eks is a widely-used official module. License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Create IAM roles, policies, OIDC providers, and assumable cross-account roles declaratively via the official terraform-aws-iam module.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model hand-writing IAM JSON drifts on trust-policy/permission-boundary semantics and cannot reconcile against live IAM state.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: The module encodes correct IAM resource patterns and terraform applies them idempotently; least-privilege structure is deterministic, not improvised.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: terraform-aws-iam has 235M+ all-time Registry downloads (most-downloaded module). License Apache-2.0.

candidates.intent: Execute the core Terraform lifecycle (init, validate, plan, apply, destroy) against a configuration with remote state locking and drift detection.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot compute a real resource diff, lock remote state, or reconcile desired vs actual infrastructure; it guesses what 'apply' would do.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: Terraform's graph engine computes a deterministic plan diff and applies it with state locking and idempotency.
candidates.verify_note: Terraform core is now BUSL-1.1 (Business Source License) since v1.6 — NOT open source; OpenTofu is the MPL-2.0 fork. Confirm license before any reliance.

candidates.intent: Run the open-source OpenTofu IaC lifecycle (init/plan/apply/destroy) — an MPL-2.0 fork of Terraform — with state encryption and provider-driven resource reconciliation.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Same as Terraform: a model cannot compute real resource diffs or reconcile state idempotently.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: OpenTofu provides a deterministic plan/apply engine under a permissive license, with built-in state encryption Terraform lacked.
candidates.verify_note: OpenTofu is the Linux-Foundation MPL-2.0 fork of Terraform created after the BUSL relicense; license MPL-2.0 confirmed by project.

candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare LLM cannot run idempotent, OS-aware package/config steps on remote hosts and verify convergence; it emits brittle shell that re-breaks on re-run.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: widely-used geerlingguy role, installs Docker on Linux. License MIT (geerlingguy roles are MIT).

candidates.intent: Install and configure Nginx (vhosts, upstreams, SSL, repo source) idempotently across RedHat/Debian/Arch/FreeBSD/OpenBSD via a packaged Ansible role.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: role installs latest Nginx from official repos across many OSes. License MIT.

candidates.intent: Install and configure PostgreSQL (cluster, users, databases, hba rules, config) idempotently via a packaged Ansible role.

candidates.intent: Install and configure MySQL/MariaDB (server, root auth, users, databases, replication) idempotently via a packaged Ansible role.

candidates.intent: Author and apply a Kubernetes Deployment + Service + HPA manifest set with rolling-update strategy, probes, and resource limits via kubectl apply.

candidates.intent: Define and bring up a multi-service application stack (services, networks, volumes, depends_on, healthchecks) via docker compose up.

candidates.intent: Run a multi-crew content-generation Flow that researches, drafts, and formats blog posts, LinkedIn posts, and research reports through coordinated agent crews.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via WebFetch: example exists. License per-example; confirm. Agentic ceiling.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via WebFetch: 'Lead Score Flow — qualifies leads with human-in-the-loop review'. License per-example; confirm.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via WebFetch + search: example performs financial analysis with SEC data. License per-example. NOT financial advice — advisory only.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via WebFetch: Recruitment example exists. License per-example. Bias/fairness review required before any HR use.

candidates.intent: Orchestrate a supervisor agent that routes a query to specialized worker agents (each a graph node), aggregates their outputs, and synthesizes a cited final answer.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare model cannot maintain graph state across multi-agent hops, route by intent, and aggregate worker outputs deterministically; it loses scratchpads between turns.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: LangGraph provides explicit stateful nodes/edges so the supervisor routing+aggregation procedure is reproducible; orchestration is the lift, reasoning stays LLM.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: supervisor multi-agent is a canonical LangGraph pattern. License MIT (langgraph). Agentic ceiling.

candidates.intent: Run a plan-and-execute agent graph: a planner node produces a step list, an executor node runs each step (with tools/RAG), and a replanner revises remaining steps based on results.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A single call cannot separate planning from execution, persist intermediate step results, or replan based on tool feedback across turns.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: The graph encodes planner/executor/replanner subgraphs with shared state for reproducible plan-then-execute; structural orchestration lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: plan-and-execute with planner/executor/RAG subgraphs is a documented LangGraph pattern. License MIT.

candidates.intent: Run a reflection agent graph where a generator node drafts, a critic node evaluates against quality criteria, and the graph loops until a quality threshold or max iterations.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A single call cannot run a bounded self-critique loop with persisted critique history and a deterministic stop condition.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: The graph encodes a generate->critique->revise loop with a deterministic termination gate; orchestration/loop control is the lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: reflection (generate/critique/route) is a named LangGraph pattern. License MIT.

candidates.intent: Run an agent graph that interrupts at a designated node to await human approval/edit, then resumes from persisted checkpoint state.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare model cannot pause mid-procedure, persist full state to a checkpoint, and resume after an out-of-band human action.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: LangGraph's checkpointer + interrupt mechanism deterministically pauses/resumes the procedure around human approval; control flow is the lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: LangGraph interrupts + HITL with checkpointers are documented. License MIT. Pause/resume mechanics are deterministic; content is not.

candidates.intent: Wrap any input->output task signature in a DSPy ChainOfThought module that elicits step-by-step reasoning before the final field, and is optimizable by a teleprompter.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: Hand-written CoT prompting is brittle and unoptimized; a model can't systematically tune its own reasoning prompt against a metric.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: DSPy abstracts CoT behind a typed signature and lets optimizers (BootstrapFewShot/MIPRO) compile better prompts/demos against a metric; the compile/optimize step is the structural lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via search + docs: ChainOfThought is a core DSPy module. License MIT (dspy). Module is a prompt program — output is LLM-generated.

candidates.intent: Implement a DSPy ReAct module that satisfies a signature by interleaving reasoning and tool calls until it can answer.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare model cannot reliably structure a reason->act->observe tool loop bounded by a step budget and a typed output contract.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: DSPy ReAct encodes the tool-use loop behind a signature and is optimizable; the loop structure and optimization are the lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via docs: 'ReAct — an agent that can use tools to implement the given signature.' License MIT.

candidates.intent: Implement a DSPy ProgramOfThought module that emits code whose execution result determines the answer (e.g., for arithmetic/data tasks).
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A bare model often miscomputes when reasoning in text; it has no guaranteed-correct execution channel.
candidates.lift_hypothesis: ProgramOfThought routes the answer through real code execution, making numeric/logic results deterministic given correct code; the execute step is the structural lift.
candidates.verify_note: Verified via docs: 'ProgramOfThought — outputs code whose execution results dictate the response.' License MIT. Code-gen leaf is LLM; execution is deterministic.

candidates.intent: Compile a DSPy program by bootstrapping few-shot demonstrations / instructions from a trainset against a metric (BootstrapFewShot, MIPRO) to raise task accuracy.
candidates.gap_hypothesis: A model cannot systematically search over prompts/demonstrations and select those that maximize a held-out metric; it can only hand-tweak.

candidates.verify_note: Verified via search: BootstrapFewShot/MIPRO/BootstrapFinetune are DSPy optimizers. License MIT. Search is structured but uses LLM evaluations.
